To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a comprehensive simulation of the power and signal domains in complex systems is feasible and (2) the interaction between signal and power domains can be significant and should be considered in the design process.
the power and the signal domain are tightly coupled in server systems.

the framework is able to simulate the signal and power domain interactions in a comprehensive manner, that the framework is scalable and can be applied to complex system level simulations, that the framework can be used for the simulation of a variety of different signal integrity scenarios, and that the nature of the power and signal domain interactions can be understood by means of simplified board level simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework that considers the power distribution network and signal lines in a comprehensive manner.
the development of simulation tools for signal and power integrity analysis.
developing a framework to enable co simulation of signal integrity and power integrity in complex systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
co simulation of signal integrity and power integrity in a system level simulation is a complex task, but that a co simulation of the two domains is possible.
a co simulation framework is necessary to capture the effects of power integrity on the signal integrity and vice versa.
a complete simulation of power and signal integrity in a server system would require the use of a multi-domain simulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the framework for co simulation of power and signal domains in server systems is a promising solution for comprehensive analysis of the system.
the framework described in this work can be utilized for comprehensive analysis of signal and power domains.
the interactions are not limited to the power domain and can be observed in the signal domain as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive simulation of power and signal domains should be performed in order to avoid the risk of false conclusions.
the signal and power integrity of high speed links are strongly related and should be considered together for a more comprehensive simulation of server systems.
power and signal domains should be considered together in a co simulation framework to accurately model the interactions and predict the performance of high speed links.
